title: A simple circuit
card: Light a bulb with a battery.

predict.prompt: The bulb is lit. What will happen if you make a gap in one of the wires?

try: Tap the switch to close the loop. Tap a wire to take it out and make a gap. Then add a second bulb.
safety: Only ever experiment with small batteries. Never play with plugs or sockets: the electricity in the walls is dangerous.
result: The bulb lit only when the loop was closed. A gap or an open switch put it out. Two bulbs in one loop both lit, but more dimly.
why: Electricity flows only round a complete loop, called a circuit: from the battery, through the wires and the bulb, and back to the battery.
A switch is a gap you can open and close. Open, it breaks the loop and the light goes out. Closed, the electricity flows again.
With two bulbs in one loop, they share the battery's push, so each glows more dimly. Wires are made of copper because metals let electricity through easily.
